# Orbit

> Orbit gives coding agents one environment contract for all of a project's microservices: they read it as JSON, start only the slice a change needs, wait for real readiness, and verify the application before reporting back.

A coding agent asked to run a project with Orbit should read the skill first. It is the canonical, machine-readable playbook: setup, the core loop, and what counts as proof that the application works.

## Agent instructions

- [Orbit skill](https://orbit.dotw.me/agent/SKILL.md): setup, core loop, verification rules
- [Workflows reference](https://orbit.dotw.me/agent/references/workflows.md): longer workflows the skill points to
- [Aspire migration](https://orbit.dotw.me/agent/references/aspire-migration.md): migrating an Aspire AppHost
- [Skill discovery index](https://orbit.dotw.me/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json)

## Docs

- [Use Orbit with your project](https://orbit.dotw.me/docs/local-first): the one request to give your agent
- [Configuration](https://orbit.dotw.me/docs/configuration): the orbit.yaml schema
- [Agent CLI contract](https://orbit.dotw.me/docs/agent-cli): the --json envelope every command returns
- [Troubleshooting](https://orbit.dotw.me/docs/troubleshooting): runtime and workflow errors

## Optional

- [Why Orbit](https://orbit.dotw.me/docs/why-orbit): design trade-offs and tool comparisons
- [Architecture](https://orbit.dotw.me/docs/architecture): state machine and event model
